look_here_first: LOOK HERE FIRST: Follow the glossy black stipe into the black rachis all the way through the narrow once-pinnate blade. Check the many small oblong pinnae, usually with a tiny upper-side basal ear (acroscopic auricle). Turn a fertile pinna over to look for 2–5 pairs of elongated sori.

morphology_keys.habit: Small perennial fern rooted in shaded rock cracks and limestone or other basic rock; fronds narrow, commonly 9–20 cm long.
morphology_keys.leaves_attachment: Frond once pinnate throughout, with roughly 20–40 pairs of oblong pinnae; margins entire to shallowly scalloped; small acroscopic auricle often present at pinna base.
morphology_keys.flower_reproductive: Ferns lack flowers. Mature pinnae bear usually 2–5 pairs of elongate sori along veins on the underside; a thin indusium covers young sori.
morphology_keys.fruit_seed: No fruit or seeds; spores develop in sporangia inside the underside sori.
morphology_keys.stem_bud: Petiole (stipe) and leaf axis (rachis) are glossy black throughout, unlike relatives with green upper rachises.

confused_with: Asplenium platyneuron (often dimorphic fertile and sterile fronds, pinnae more often alternate; compare frond bases and rachis)
Asplenium trichomanes (rounder, shorter pinnae; compare pinna outline and basal auricle)
Adiantum capillus-veneris (fan-shaped pinnules and marginal sori rather than narrow oblong pinnae with underside linear sori)
comparisons.key_distinctions: Combine continuous black rachis, narrow one-pinnate blade, many oblong pinnae with a small upper basal ear, and paired linear sori beneath pinnae. Do not identify from dark stalk color alone.
